title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Adds robust lifecycle controls for streaming responses: explicit client cancel handling (graceful stop + KV cache retention), deterministic server-side timeouts and cancellation propagation, improved disconnect detection and reconnect/resume flow with client-provided resume tokens, and OpenAI-compatibility plumbing for stream control events and function/tool-calling consistency. Motivation: production incidents showed dangling goroutines and partial KV cache corruption when clients cancelled mid-stream or disconnected under flappy networks. This PR standardizes a lifecycle state machine (started, streaming, cancelled-client, deadline-exceeded, disconnected, resumed, finished) and introduces a compact resume token that encodes stream id, key-version, and last-ack offset. The change touches runtime streaming manager, transport layer, openai compatibility adapter, Python SDK streaming helpers, and docs. Includes unit and integration tests that simulate client cancel, abrupt TCP disconnects, reconnect with resume token, server-enforced timeouts, and function call resumability. Backwards compatibility: old clients will continue to receive legacy stream events but will not benefit from resume tokens. OpenAI-compatible clients will get identical control event framing ("[DONE]" and explicit status events) and a new "resume_token" field in the final control frame when resume is supported. Checklist: 1) implement lifecycle state transitions and cancellation propagation; 2) add resume token generation/validation; 3) wire OpenAI compat event frames; 4) add metrics for cancelled/timeout/resumed streams; 5) update SDKs and docs; 6) run canary for 48h. Testing notes: simulated partial write failures and race windows with goroutine leak detector enabled. Observability: added per-stream metrics (stream_lifecycle_state_count, stream_resume_attempts_total, stream_resume_success_total, stream_cancel_latency_ms). Operational notes: default server timeout lowered to 60s from 90s for streaming requests, configurable via STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Migration: no schema changes, no customer action required. See commits and review comments for implementation details.

review_comments: Ravi: Nice cleanup of the state machine. Two concerns: 1) race between client cancel and server timeout needs a deterministic winner, please add a test asserting cancellation precedence; 2) ensure resume tokens are compact and signed to avoid replay attacks.
Author (Ava): Added deterministic ordering: client cancel wins if received before server timeout handler fires; added HMAC-signed resume tokens with TTL. Added tests for race and replay.

merge_commit_message: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect/resume with OpenAI compat\n\nAdds lifecycle state machine, resume tokens, server timeouts, SDK helpers, metrics, and docs.
release_notes: Improved streaming stability: client cancel is now handled deterministically and leaves KV cache in a consistent state.
Reconnect/resume support: clients may resume interrupted streams using resume tokens (OpenAI-compatible control frames).
Operational change: default STREAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS lowered to 60s (configurable).
New metrics: stream_lifecycle_state_count, stream_resume_attempts_total, stream_resume_success_total, stream_cancel_latency_ms.
